heading_en: Positioning of Closing Brackets, Full Stops, Commas and Middle Dots at Line End
heading_ja: 行末に配置する終わり括弧類，句点類，読点類及び​中点類の​配置方法

cases.quote: In principle, closing brackets (cl-02), commas (cl-07) or full stops (cl-06) at the line end have half em spacing after them (see Figure 76). This half em spacing can be removed for line adjustment (for more about line adjustment, see § 3.8 Line Adjustment ). However, the possibilities are only half em spacing or solid. Other spacing, such as quarter em spacing should not be used.
cases.rationale: §D.1's own legend already reads this rule at cl-02 (closing bracket) x line-end, where Table 4 stays rigid because JIS X 4051's own convention never pads that boundary in the first place (`D.1/closing-bracket-at-line-end/table-4-protects-what-table-3-and-5-drain`'s own rationale states that coordinate). §3.1.9's own text draws no distinction among its three named classes at all — its opening sentence treats "closing brackets (cl-02), commas (cl-07) or full stops (cl-06)" identically, every one of them carrying a half em that "can be removed for line adjustment" — so a case for this rule at the full stop's own coordinate needs no textual difference from D.1's own coordinate to earn its place: §D.1 and §3.1.9 are two different rule addresses, and the coverage this suite counts is per address, not per amount. What does distinguish cl-06 from the other two classes this rule names, worth stating because a reader moving from §B.2 note 2 and note 6 to this rule might otherwise expect an identical shape at every one of the three coordinates, is §B.2 note 6's own parenthetical: JIS X 4051 keeps the full stop's own half em and withdraws only the comma's, so cl-06 is the one class of this rule's three whose JIS X 4051 reading is never solid at all. Table 1 states `1/2 be` for cl-06 at the line end, citing that note; the three reduction tables read exactly as `D.1.json`'s own cl-02 entries do — `spec/captured/table3.en.tsv` reads `1/2=0 stage 2`, `table4.en.tsv` reads a bare `1/2` (rigid, no reduction opportunity at all), and `table5.en.tsv` reads `1/2=0 stage 2` again — but not for the identical reason D.1's own legend gives at cl-02. §D.1's own text contrasts the two explicitly ("On the other hand"): cl-02 and cl-07 stay rigid under Table 4 because JIS X 4051 never pads that boundary at all (`table4.en.tsv`'s cl-02×line-end cell reads blank), while cl-06 stays rigid because JIS X 4051 does pad it with a half em and its own convention simply refuses to let that padding reduce for line adjustment (`table4.en.tsv`'s cl-06×line-end cell reads a bare `1/2`, not blank). Table 4 alone stays rigid here, which is the fact worth a case of its own: an implementation that reduces this boundary under every table it recognizes, without checking whether the selected table is JIS X 4051's own, answers Table 4 wrong in the direction that discards a real, load-bearing rigidity. The `discrete` shape on the two reducible tables is this rule's own second half read directly: "the possibilities are only half em spacing or solid" states a two-valued drain rather than a continuous one, matching `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/evaluate.rs`'s own `cell_reduction`, which reads the `=` token as `Reduction::Discrete` and the `-` token as `Reduction::Range` — the same decoder `D.1.json`'s own `1/2=0 stage 2` cell and `D.2/middle-dot-at-line-end`'s own `1/4-0 stage 3` cell already pin from opposite sides of that distinction.

permitted.source: JLReq §3.1.9, Table 3 (JLReq's own adopted method, §D preamble)

JLReq §3.1.9, Table 4 (JIS X 4051's own convention, §D preamble) — rigid, but not for the same reason §D.1's own legend gives at cl-02: JIS X 4051 pads this boundary with a half em and then refuses to let that padding reduce for line adjustment (§D.1: "which is not allowed to reduce this spacing"), rather than never padding it at all
JLReq §3.1.9, Table 5 (a third method found in other publications, §D preamble)

forbidden.why: §3.1.9 states in so many words that "the possibilities are only half em spacing or solid" and that "other spacing, such as quarter em spacing should not be used" — a continuously-shrinking reading is exactly the intermediate value this sentence forbids, and none of the three permitted entries above answers `range`: Table 3 and Table 5 both drain this space discretely, all at once, and Table 4 does not drain it at all.
